context: a letter from J. V. Carus, which you are answering
exchanges:
I get in this moment the sheets T, U, X, Y, or p 273–336. Unfortunately the sheet S or p. 257–272 is still wanting. I hasten to tell it to you at once. I apply to you, as the envelop bears the stamp “Bromley” and I therefore conclude that you were sending the sheets.

Pray send the missing as soon as possible   Believe me | Yours most truly | J. Victor Carus

Leipzig, 39, Elsterstrasse

7 Oct 67

I am sorry you have had so much trouble. I cannot imagine how the sheet could have been lost unless opened by the post office, or unless I sent the sheet by mistake to France or Russia in which case I hope it will be returned & it shall be sent to you.

In the meantime I send by this post a corrected revise which I trust will serve your purpose—

Dear Sir | yours very sincerely | Ch. Darwin
